title: The Memory of the Staircase
poemText: I am an old wooden staircase in a Parisian building

The light steps of the lover taking them two at a time
The hesitant little steps of the child learning to walk
The slow steps of the old lady afraid of falling
I have felt the weight of moving days
Furniture going up full of hope
Furniture going down full of sadness
I drank the tears that fell on my steps
I heard the laughter echoing in my stairwell
I am the silent witness to a hundred years of life
And if one day they destroy me
Will keep within it the scent of a step

To cling to the feet of its owner

title: The Merchant of Maybe
poemText: He has his little stall in an alley
People come to see him when they are at the end of their rope
When life has left them nothing but grey certainty
Just enough to hold on one more day
Just enough to open a small window
In the wall of their despair
But he has the finest of trades
He is a sower of fertile doubts
In the arid field of reality.

Bringing with it a scent of yesteryear
The other words look at it with suspicion
For he knows that words never truly die
And that a little love is enough
And restore their place in the world.

Their smiles are masks of rain
The stationmaster is an old man
Who lost his own love here fifty years ago
He whistles the departure with a whistle of tears
Carrying with it halves of lives
And on the platform only silence remains
Of someone who has just left

title: The Thief of Horizons
poemText: He would arrive at night with large fog scissors
And he cut out the horizon
And carried it away in his sack
In the morning people woke up
And the sky touched the earth
There was no far away anymore
The world was a little box with no way out
People stopped looking out the window
And they found that life was very small
Until the day a child took a blue pencil
A simple line between the earth and the sky
And the thief died of hunger
For he fed only on lost hopes.

title: Blue, the Color of Dreams
poemText: I am not a color that screams
I am a great murmur, a sigh
The color of that which is far away
The horizon, the sea, and the vein on a hand
I am the color of escape
The immense sky that belongs to no one
And where the birds draw poems of freedom
I am the deep ocean full of voyages and monsters
The liquid road to unknown islands
I am the uniform of the sailor who is leaving
And the color of the eyes in which one drowns in love
I am the color of dreams and of hope
The blue smoke of a wood fire rising to the stars
The ink of the letter one is waiting for
And the little flame of the gas in the silent night
But I am also the color of sorrow
The "blues" of the black musician in a Chicago bar
The color of lips when one is cold
The terrible blue of a bruise on the skin and on the soul
I am the color of the work uniform
The "bleu de travail" that smells of sweat and fatigue
The faded blue of a life spent in a factory
Looking at the sky through a dirty window
I am the greatest of paradoxes
The color of the cage and of freedom
I am the blue of the worker's overalls
And the blue of the sky he looks at while dreaming
I am the distance between what one is
And what one would like to be
I am the color of the human soul
A great sea of desires and of melancholy.

title: Green, the Color of Hope
poemText: I am not a hurried color
I am patience, I am perseverance
The little blade of grass that grows through the concrete
The ivy that slowly climbs the wall of time
I am the great quiet breath of the forests
I am the color of hope
The first bud on the dead tree of winter
The four-leaf clover found by a child
The green light at the crossroads that says "Go, live your life"
I am the fresh mint in a glass of water
The little motionless lizard on the warm stone
And the deep green of a mountain lake
I am the repose of the eye and the calm of the heart
The promise that even after the harshest of winters
But men have invented another life for me
They took my name to put it on their money
That paper that buys everything except happiness
They put me on the uniforms of their soldiers
And on the gambling table where fortunes are lost
I have become the color of jealousy
The murky green of envy in the eyes
The color of absinthe that drives one mad
And of the mold on forgotten bread
They have created a green that is the enemy of life
A green of poison, a green of dollars, a green of profit
There are two greens in the world
The one that liberates and the one that imprisons
And every day you must choose
Between the grass in the park where you can lie down to do nothing
And the banknote you must earn to survive.

title: Red, the Color of the Heart
poemText: After the silence of white and black
I am the first color, the great scream
The color that even the blind can feel
The warmth of blood on the skin
I am the color of life and of desire
The cherry that one steals from the tree
The lips of a woman waiting for a kiss
The fragile and stubborn poppy in the wheat field
The heart drawn in chalk on a gray wall
I am the wine of lovers and the blush of shyness
The blood that runs in the veins
The proof that one is alive
But I am also the color of anger and of war
The fire that devours the house
The blood that flows on the pavement
The face of an angry man
The teacher's pen that crosses out mistakes
The stop sign that kills movement
And the flag of the revolution
I am a paradox, a wound and a flower
The most joyful and the most terrible of colors
I am the velvet curtain of the theater
And the stain on the butcher's apron
I am the candy apple of the funfair
And the light of the brothel in the night
I am the color of all passions
From love to hate there is only one step
And that step is always red
A world without me would be a reasonable world

title: Yellow, the Color of Laughter
poemText: I am the color of laughter and of the sun
I am simple joy, a color without manners
That bursts forth in the middle of the serious green of the meadow
A million dandelions applauding the spring
I am the sharp and sour taste of the lemon
The heat of mustard that rushes to the nose
The liquid heart of a fried egg
I am the naive sunflower that follows its god the sun
And the raincoat of a child jumping in puddles
I am a party, a surprise, an exclamation
But you must not trust my smile
I am also a color that lies
The color of sickness on a man's skin
The yellow and feverish light of a tired lightbulb
The pages of an old book that are slowly dying
I am the color of betrayal and of cowardice
At the crossroads I am the middle light
The one that is neither yes nor no
The one that says "Careful, maybe danger"
I am the desert sand where one dies of thirst
And the fake gold of a cheap ring
That leaves a green trace on the finger
I am joy, but a joy that knows it does not last
The beauty of summer just before autumn
A laughter that is on the verge of tears
I am the most cheerful and the most unsettling of colors
Before the shadow comes to take it all back.

title: White, the Color of Everything and Nothing
poemText: They say I am not a color
That I am the absence, the blank page, the great nothing
But it is I who begins everything
I am the milk of the world's first morning
The first tooth of a smiling child
The fresh snow that offers forgiveness to a dirty city
I am the bride's dress full of fragile promises
And the blank page of the new notebook where everything is still possible
I am the dove of peace that does not exist
And the sail of the boat leaving for the horizon
I am innocence and the beginning
The first word of a poem
But I am also the other thing
The thing one does not speak of
I am the white wall of the hospital that smells of fear
The white flag of the lost battle
The white silence after the scream
I am the bone polished by time and vultures
The blinding white light of the interrogation
And the white face of the returning ghost
I am the void and the end
The last word of an erased poem
I am the best and the worst
The nuptial bed and the shroud
The cloud where one sees an angel's face
And the fog where one gets lost forever
I am the sugar and the salt
I do not choose a side
I am just there, before and after
The great silence where all colors are born

title: The Swifts

the façade the gutters the plaster

title: The Silence in the Library
poemText: On the library door hangs a sign
and the woman at the desk puts a finger to her lips
as in a room where someone is sleeping
it is the loudest place in town
louder than the square on market day
only it is heard with the eyes
here a thousand voices speak at once
poets dead a hundred years speak
and complain and laugh and cry out
you open a book and the talking begins
here is the storm here is the war
here someone whispers I love you
here a ship goes down and no one hears
except you with your finger on the line
the woman at the desk knows it best
that is why she makes this silence
not so that people should be quiet
but so that those may be heard
who can no longer speak any other way
she wants everyone to be able to speak
the dead and the living all at once
and that is only possible in silence
and so the library is full of uproar
full of singing and weeping and laughter
under the sign that says SILENCE PLEASE
and silence is not the ban on speaking
so that at last everyone can

title: The Taxi Driver Who Turns Off the Meter

title: The Summer Cinema Projectionist

the most faithful audience in the world

the actress's trunk that weighs more than the actress

title: The Staircase without a Lift
poemText: House number twelve has no lift
and on every floor two lives
On the ground floor the lady who bakes
her scent rises free of charge
all the way to the fourth
on the first the man with the cello
On the second the young couple
they take the stairs two at a time going up
three at a time coming down
once they carried a pram up
and since then they count the steps too
the steps outside it are the quietest
And on the fourth Mr Gregory
half an hour to the top
at the baking lady's floor he breathes in
at the young couple's he smiles
at the empty flat he takes off his hat
And Mr Gregory shakes his head
on the ground floor I'd be home at once
This way it takes me an hour to come home
and on the way I meet the whole house
the scent the music the children the silence
The young ones run the stairs in a minute
I know every step by name
the step where I start taking off my shoes
A lift would carry me up fast
that over four floors is learning

title: Indian Summer
poemText: like someone who keeps turning around
A silver thread above the stubble
a second thread across the lane
a third one lands on your sleeve
that's the spiders moving summer out
They wrap it in silver paper
and send it off by wind
wasps stagger in the fallen pears
and the swallows sit on the wires
at the end of a song
It doesn't end says the grandfather
that's summer taking its leave of you

through the hole in the greenhouse roof
a patch of blue is already shining

title: The Melting Snowman
poemText: He stood by the gate since December
a carrot in the middle of his face
and a broom under his arm
like a soldier guarding the garden
In March he began to lose weight
all that was left on the lawn
where the grass is greener than anywhere else
Did he die? asks the child
Snow doesn't die says the grandfather
right now it lives in the brook
in summer it will be a cloud
and in December it will come back
The child gathers up the carrot
and puts them away in a shoebox
I'm keeping his things for him

title: The First Whistle
poemText: Grandfather can whistle like a blackbird
and even for the waiter in the café
and that is exactly why he does it
and nothing comes from his lips but air
the boy purses his mouth like grandfather
blow like you don't want to wake your mother
and the tears are not far off
grandfathers are never in a hurry
that is why grandsons love them
he peels an apple and says
it took me a whole summer to learn
and in the end a blackbird taught me
because he kept laughing at me
between one nothing and the next nothing
The boy is startled by his own mouth
because the blackbird on the fence

title: The First Grey Hair
poemText: In the morning at the bathroom mirror
between the brushes and the bottles
between the steam and the hurry
white as a thread from another sweater
in the middle of all that dark brown
the tweezers wait on the shelf
executions are held in the morning
The man stands in the doorway with his coffee
I've got my first grey hair
And the man takes a sip of coffee
it grew on you that winter
when the little one was sick
and you didn't sleep for three nights
and every morning you told me
the tweezers stay on the shelf

the cat watches from the windowsill

that up there above her ceiling
there is right now a summer
the soup has boiled over a little

and pushes the cake towards her son
because they hear a dead man
she has known it for a long time
but it only knows how to give back

title: The Sides of the Bed
poemText: he slept on the door side
There was never a vote on it
since the first night in the rented room
in case a child cried in the night
in case the world got a bad idea
it would have to get past him first
because she liked hearing the rain
each their own hollow in the mattress
his detective novels and nose drops
without a word they changed sides
mum dad have you gone mad
Only the burglars don't come anymore
the door has been quiet for years
the children cry in other cities
through the window now at night
something bigger than a burglar looks in
for forty years he stood between her and the world

title: The Proofreader
poemText: forty years of other people's mistakes
sentences that set out and never arrived
words split in the worst possible place
She has corrected novels and train timetables
and not one of them was hers
on the last page it says
But the wife has been dead thirty years
it says so in the very first chapter
The proofreader raises her red pencil
The pencil hangs a moment over the paper
like a wasp over a glass
And then the proofreader erases her mark
the only one in forty years
the past tense and the present tense
the tense of those who are gone
and read over your shoulder anyway
and some are left to live

poemText: Every evening she sings to the children

for the room so it remembers the tune

who always used to fall asleep
in the middle of the second verse
and all her life has wanted to know

title: The Last Night Flight
poemText: The airport at one in the morning
the departure board has played its last hand
the perfume shop sleeps behind its grille
the coffee machine keeps its light on
The cleaning woman rides her machine
across a hall as big as a town square
even the sniffer dog is asleep
Only the tower is still lit
and across the screen a dot is traveling
And the controller watches the dot
and wonders who is sitting in it
maybe a woman flying to a funeral
rehearsing her first sentence in silence
maybe a man coming home after twenty years
afraid he's forgotten the name of his street
maybe a child flying for the first time
asleep with its forehead on the window
above a land full of small lights
And for that one little dot
the whole airport lights up again
the runway the hall the belts
and the sign ARRIVALS above the doors
because no one is allowed to land in the dark
and no one in this world

title: The Hitchhiker with a Sign Saying Anywhere
poemText: At the edge of the road past the last house

and on it in big letters
That's not a direction young man
It's the best direction in the world
the only one you can't miss
I'm only going as far as Slough
but the driver is already rolling up his window
Slough suddenly seems very small to him
A second car stops a third a fifth
and they all ask the same thing
and the hitchhiker lifts his sign a little higher
I'm only going to my mother-in-law's
and each one in his rearview mirror
carries away a piece of that word
Toward evening an old car pulls over

says the hitchhiker and gets in

and for the first time all day

title: The Road that Led Nowhere
poemText: Past the village a road begins
with an avenue of old cherry trees
and a little bridge over the brook
It starts out grandly like all roads do
in the middle of the oats
like a sentence someone never finished
Once they say it was meant to reach a town
or a bridge that changed its mind
the plans went yellow in the district archive

a road without a destination shall be cancelled
it says so in the regulations
but there was never money for that
and so it keeps on leading
lovers because they meet no one there
an old man with a cane because he has nowhere to get to
a lady with a dog that chases wind through the oats
children on bikes riding to the end of the world
and home in time for supper

to work to the office to the train
only this one is in no hurry at all
and that is why it walks so well

from all the people standing there looking

title: The Boundary Stone
poemText: On the bank between Upper End and Lower End
a stone sits in the grass
a U carved on one side
an L carved on the other

the mayors took the meadow to court
the farmers brawled at the parish fair

the Upper End cow grazes Lower End grass

a tin shed a great wheel
and a sign saying END OF THE LINE
beyond there is nothing at all
and the wind that has lived here forever

he greets the cabins like old acquaintances
and all day long he answers

eat their sandwiches on the sheltered side of the shed

looking at the ridge above the station

up there you can only walk
higher still you can only look
Everything in this world stretches only as far as it will
he says screwing his thermos shut
they always stop a little short of the summit
the last stretch everyone must climb alone
it can only be stood in silence

title: The Man Who Came Back the Same Way
poemText: Every morning at ten past seven
down Station Street across the footbridge
past the bakery and past the church
and at five in the afternoon
back along the very same way
man at least buy yourself a bicycle
you'll wear a groove in that one

in the evening other people's dinners drifted from open windows
in the morning the church was on his right hand
in the evening on his left
on Monday there was a puddle on the footbridge
on Tuesday it had turned into a mirror
in spring the lilacs overtook him on the way
in winter he walked in his own morning footprints

I have never once in my life
in the morning a man goes down it
who doesn't yet know how the day will end
in the evening a man comes back
they walk on the same stones
and each takes a different road

he said taking the boy's hand

under the old glasses and the bills

title: The Postcard that Arrived Years Late
poemText: When they took apart the old sorting machine at the post office
a postcard fell out from behind the tin
the sea a lighthouse two sailboats
and a postmark thirty years old
and where she has moved to

what has once been written must arrive

the house was rebuilt strange names on the doorbells
after a week he finally tracked down
in another town by a park
he went there on a Sunday
on a ticket he paid for himself
he said and handed him the postcard

and read for a very long time
She never came back you know
But she wrote that she would

on his night table sea side out
and from that evening on he went on waiting
only no longer just like that
now he had it in writing

the garden the line the wind

her first step in forty years

the way you sleep when the work is done

title: Radio for the Sleepless
poemText: At two in the morning a voice speaks on the radio
The baker woman listens already up
the watchman listens not yet in bed
the mother with a child on her shoulder
the truck driver between two towns
the old man whose bed is too big
and the boy afraid to switch off the light
None of them knows about the others
I am the last person awake in the world
and the voice on the radio speaks
as if sitting in each of their rooms
I don't actually know if you're out there
in twenty years nobody has written to me
so I'll ask you just one thing
turn your light on for a moment
And the host steps to the studio window
here and there and over there too
by the station on the ground floor under the tower
a whole constellation of the sleepless
Good night he says into the microphone
and for the first time in twenty years
he isn't saying it to the dark

title: The Alarm Clock that Didn't Ring on Sunday
poemText: Mr Walter has a tin alarm clock
with the little key at the back
two turns not a hair more

because Mr Walter forgets to switch it off
and then lies with his eyes closed
listening to the bells of Saint James
there was a party at the neighbour's
accordion wine stories of the old days
and Mr Walter came home late
and fell asleep in his shoes
On Sunday he woke at nine
the sun already sat on the floor
like a guest nobody had invited
then looked at the alarm clock
You could have told me sooner
that there's no ringing on Sundays
doesn't wind it on Saturday nights
and on Sunday mornings he lies in
listening to the bells of Saint James

title: The Minute of Silence
poemText: At the stadium across the river
let us observe a minute of silence
chalked the lines of this pitch
And five thousand people stood up
For the referee it lasted exactly a minute
For the goalkeeper it lasted one penalty
the one Mr Josef once saved
the only one of his life
For the boys on the terraces it lasted forever
because boys don't know how to stand still
For the sausage seller it was short
he'd barely taken off his cap
For the widow in row twelve
she walked the whole length of it
and still had some left over
And for the pigeons on the grandstand roof
Then the referee blew his whistle
and the ball set off across the grass
the silence sat down in the empty seat
and watched the match to the end

title: The Last Day of the Holidays

and short as nothing at all
so from morning on he's rushing
one last time to the river
one last time up the cherry tree
though the cherries are long gone
one last ride on his bike in a single go
out to the transformer and back
the afternoon blinks and is gone
and the evening smells of September

sitting by the door like a dog
that knows tomorrow means the vet
come home we're up early tomorrow
and that tomorrow is a longer word
is just the day before the first
that once they too could hear

so that evening in his pencil case
he hides a pebble from the river
what did you do this summer

poemText: The dead can't smell the flowers
kneeling with his hands in the earth
the dead don't mind the weeds
a woman with a shopping bag
The pansies are lovely this year
Because a man in a hat comes
and sits down by the begonias
The flowers are not for the dead
the flowers are for the living
so they have somewhere to come
and a time to come back
Mr Victor is not a gardener

poemText: In the village they had a bell
that rang noon and the Angelus and the death knell
and the ringer Frank knew it
and Frank rang it one last time
Since then the church tower has been silent
but the cannon made from that bell
there was always something in the barrel
